answer: No. Your records show you were checked for a clot in your lung, but none was found. On 8 July 2025 you had a chest pain episode and a D-dimer blood test that was raised (0.92, normal is 0.49 or below). A raised D-dimer is not specific and can happen for many reasons, so you then had a CT scan of the chest vessels the same evening. The report says there was no pulmonary embolism, your lungs were clear, and there was no fluid around the lungs or heart. The only finding was mild wear-and-tear changes in the spine of your upper back. Your record lists pulmonary embolism as 'ruled out'. The chest wall pain was recorded as resolved by 22 July 2025.
short: A CT angiogram of the chest on 2025-07-08, done after a raised D-dimer, showed no pulmonary embolism; the diagnosis is recorded as ruled out.

knowledge.says: CT pulmonary angiography is the standard test to confirm or exclude a pulmonary embolism; a negative result in a good-quality study effectively rules it out.

knowledge.says: D-dimer is sensitive but not specific; it rises with many conditions, so a positive result needs imaging.
